Carries all SIX stock buckets per (MATNR, WERKS, LGORT) -- unrestricted (LABST), QI (INSME), blocked (SPEME), in transfer (UMLME), restricted (EINME), returns (RETME) -- typed NUMERIC, plus ERSDA (segment creation date; drives the as-at creation guard) and LFGJA/LFMON = last-movement period (INTEGER; dormant-stock detection). SCOPE IS HETEROGENEOUS and disclosed: PR is PLANT-scoped (EBAN has no BUKRS; use werks), Invoices are the whole company code (BSIK has no WERKS). Reuses the canonical open-item logic of each leg (never re-derived):
  * Open Invoices (BSIK) — booked EUR via **DMBTR** (company-code currency,
    ties to the GL / FBL1N), NOT a spot-FX of the document amount; SHKZG-
    signed so a genuine payable is negative. `exclude_intercompany` (default
    True) drops IC vendors via the shared registry.
  * Open PO (EKKO/EKPO/EKBE) — sum(open_commitment_value) per currency;
    `exclude_scheduling_agreements` (default True, BSTYP<>'L') and
    `include_delivery_complete` (default False, ELIKZ) passed through.
  * Open PR (EBAN) — MENGE*PREIS/PEINH over open reqs (EBELN=''/LOEKZ=''/
    EBAKZ<>'X'). EBAN has no BUKRS — it is PLANT-scoped, so PR is disclosed
    as plant-scoped (use `werks`), not company-code-attributable.

to one plant (invoices cannot be plant-filtered — BSIK has no WERKS — so the
invoice leg is the whole company code; the mixed scope is disclosed).

gross->excluded->net reconciling amount (never silently folded). `as_of`
(ISO) effective-dates the intercompany exclusion.

Currency-native: PR/PO foreign-currency lines are reported separately (NOT
in total_liability_eur), to be converted at a stated indicative rate if a
single blended figure is wanted. Invoices are already EUR (DMBTR). Returns a
scalar summary dict (like pa_po_value_summary), NOT a table handle.

A no-match / ambiguous project returns found=False with guidance (not a crash). proj + prps + coep required (coep must hold the project's OBJNRs, else a missing_extract with the exact objnr_in hint). tools.description: Per-currency intercompany reconciliation between two entities: A's open AR to B (BSID where bukrs=bukrs_a) vs B's open AP to A (BSIK where bukrs=bukrs_b). Specify which counterparty numbers belong to each side ONE of two ways (not both): (1) registry labels group_a + group_b (the IC group_label), with F19 effective-dating via as_of; or (2) explicit numbers a_lifnrs (A's LIFNRs, in B's books) + b_kunnrs (B's KUNNRs, in A's books), which bypasses the registry. pa_reconcile_intercompany — B6 (v0.0.110). For two intercompany
entities A and B, reconciles per currency:
  - A's open AR to B: BSID rows in A's books posted to B's IC KUNNRs
  - B's open AP to A: BSIK rows in B's books posted to A's IC LIFNRs

Args:
  bukrs_a / bukrs_b
    SAP company codes — the books we're reading. Required.

There are TWO ways to specify which counterparty numbers belong to
each side. Supply EXACTLY one pairing mode:

  (1) group_a / group_b  —  registry-label mode
    IC-registry group_labels identifying each entity's LIFNR/KUNNR
    set. Must be distinct. group_label is the entity identity column
    on `pa_common.intercompany_lifnrs` / `_kunnrs`; the F12
    entity-orchestrator (`pa_admin_register_ic_entity`) is the typical
    registration path. NOTE (I-09): in production the seeded registry
    rows carry an empty group_label, so this mode can't address a
    single entity pair until the registry is curated — use mode (2)
    meanwhile.

  (2) a_lifnrs / b_kunnrs  —  explicit-number mode
    The IC counterparty numbers for each side, supplied directly:
    `a_lifnrs` = A's vendor (LIFNR) numbers as they appear in B's
    books; `b_kunnrs` = B's customer (KUNNR) numbers as they appear
    in A's books. Bypasses the group_label lookup entirely, so a
    reconcile runs even when the registry's group_label is empty or
    wrong (I-09). Robust to a broken registry; the analyst owns
    correctness of the numbers.

  as_of
    ISO YYYY-MM-DD reporting date. In registry-label mode this filters
    the IC-registry lookup through the F19 effective-dating columns.
    Ignored in explicit-number mode (the numbers are taken as given).
    Defaults to current_date when empty.

tools.name: pa_table_join
tools.description: Join two of your handles (inner/left/right/full) on shared join keys, as a new handle. args.left_handle + args.right_handle + args.on (list of join key columns present in both). how defaults to inner. select_left / select_right project subsets; suffix appended to right-side non-join columns that collide with a left output name. Both inputs touched, output new. source_extracts is the union of both inputs (later timestamp wins on key collisions). Cross-user joins refused. Spec: docs/v2-companion-tools.md §3.3.

inputSchema.description:
pa_table_join — combine two handles on shared join columns.

Spec: docs/v2-companion-tools.md §3.3.

Both handles must belong to the calling user (cross-user joins are
refused — surfaces as invalid_args). `on` lists the join key columns;
every key must exist on both sides. `select_left` / `select_right`
default to "all columns" on the respective side; specify lists to
project. Output collisions (a non-join column with the same name on
both sides) get `suffix` appended to the right-side column.

The output handle's source_extracts is the union of both inputs'
source_extracts; on key collisions the later timestamp wins (per the
lineage doc §4.3 — a join can't see fresher than its freshest
component).

tools.name: pa_table_to_xlsx
tools.description: Stream a handle's underlying table to an .xlsx file on the substrate host and return a download URL. Files live 7 days (configurable via PA_FILE_TTL_DAYS). Optional `filename` is sanitised + prepended as an analyst label to the system-generated tail (tool_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hash>.xlsx). openpyxl write_only mode + server-side cursor stream rows so wide / tall tables don't load fully in memory. Download requires the same X-Punch-Auth key as /tools and re-checks ownership against pa_common.file_registry. Spec: docs/v2-companion-tools.md §3.4.

inputSchema.description:
pa_table_to_xlsx — stream a handle's underlying table to an .xlsx
file on the substrate host and return its path + download URL.

Files live 7 days by default (configurable via PA_FILE_TTL_DAYS). The
result carries BOTH `local_path` (the on-disk path,
C:\Claude\punch_analytics_files\<user>\<file>.xlsx) and `download_url`
(/files/<filename>, same-host auth). The WHOLE file is written server-side,
so a caller co-located with the host should READ `local_path` DIRECTLY with
its file tools — O(1) model tokens for any size; never paginate the rows
back through the model. Off-host callers use download_url.

`filename` is an OPTIONAL analyst-supplied prefix that gets sanitised
and prepended to the system-generated tail (which carries the tool
name + timestamp + args-hash for collision resistance). If you don't
set it, the filename is fully system-generated. Spec:
docs/v2-companion-tools.md §3.4.

tools.name: pa_compose_pipeline_xlsx
tools.description: Compose a multi-sheet .xlsx from a list of table-handles — one sheet per handle, titled by sheet_name. Typical workflow: analyst runs a sequence of filter/aggregate/join calls (the 'pipeline') producing several handles, then composes them into one xlsx for a board pack. With the B12 rename DSL, each sheet's columns can carry human-readable headers. Ownership is re-checked per handle (one cross-user handle aborts the whole compose). Lineage is the UNION of every constituent handle's source_extracts. Sheet-name duplicates rejected up front (Excel caps at 31 chars; truncation-collisions are caught too). v2-substrate rewrite of v1's compose_pipeline_xlsx (B6, 2 of 3).

PipelineSheetSpec.description:
One sheet in a pipeline-xlsx composition. `handle` is the table-handle
to stream; `sheet_name` is the analyst-readable sheet title (capped at
31 chars, Excel's limit).
PipelineSheetSpec.title: PipelineSheetSpec

inputSchema.description:
pa_compose_pipeline_xlsx — compose a multi-sheet .xlsx from a list
of table-handles. The v2-substrate rewrite of v1's
compose_pipeline_xlsx; B6 (1 of 3 tools — reconcile_intercompany was 1
of 3 in v0.0.110, this is 2 of 3, render_trend_chart remains).

The "pipeline" name reflects the typical workflow: the analyst runs a
sequence of filter/aggregate/join/etc. calls producing several
handles (the "pipeline"), then composes them into one xlsx for a
board pack. With B12's `rename` DSL, the per-sheet column headers can
be analyst-friendly ("Vendor Name", "Amount") rather than SAP-native.

Args:
  sheets
    Ordered list of `{sheet_name, handle}` specs. Each handle must
    be owned by the caller; ownership is re-checked per handle (a
    single cross-user handle aborts the whole compose with an
    invalid_args error). Sheet names are de-duplicated server-side
    (Excel rejects duplicate sheet titles; the de-dup just renames
    the offending later sheets with a numeric suffix).

  filename
    Optional analyst-supplied prefix on the generated filename.

  include_header / freeze_header
    Same semantics as pa_table_to_xlsx; applied uniformly to every
    sheet.
